an abstract class is like a class that can have some actual code and data in it, but also can leave some methods unfinished for the child classes to do. an interface is more like a contract, it says what methods a class should have, without being the main class itself. um, depending on the language interfaces can have some implementation too now, but generally thats the difference i remember.
an abstract class is a class where you can have methods that arent implemented yet, and subclasses have to do those parts. thats the main thing i know, i dont remember the interface side very well.

an interface is basically a class that already contains the full implementation, while an abstract class is only for declaring variables and it cant have methods, so the interface does most of the actual work.

so an abstract class and an interface are both used when you kind of want different classes to follow some common structure, but they arent exactly the same. an abstract class can have normal methods with code in them, fields or state, and also abstract methods where you basically say this needs to exist but the subclass has to implement it. so you use it when the classes are pretty closely related and you want to share some common behavior. an interface is more like saying okay, anything that implements this has to provide these operations, and it usually doesnt represent the shared state of the objects. also in some languages interfaces can have default methods now so the old explanation that they can never contain code isnt always true. i think the big idea is abstract class is more of a shared base with some implementation, interface is more like a capability or contract, and a class can often implement multiple interfaces whereas inheritance from classes is more restricted depending on the language.

```python
def max_subarray(nums):
    current = best = nums[0]
    for x in nums[1:]:
        current = max(x, current + x)
        best = max(best, current)
    return best
```

```python
def max_subarray(nums):
    current = best = 0
    for x in nums:
        current = max(0, current + x)
        best = max(best, current)
    return best
```
